title: How am I using my soul?
hookLine: ask often: what am I using my soul for right now? (Meditations 5.11)
carry: what am I using it for

lines: HOW AM I USING MY SOUL?
cards: Your phone has a battery screen that shows exactly where the power went. Maps, twelve percent. Messages, twenty.
That one game, a slightly embarrassing forty. Nobody has a screen like that for attention, or for the inner life. If you did, what would today's breakdown say?
Marcus Aurelius didn't have the screen, but he had the question, and he wrote it down as a short, sharp check.

teach.h: WHAT AM I USING MY SOUL FOR NOW?
teach.b: What am I using my soul for right now? Marcus writes this in book five, entry eleven, and says to ask it on every occasion. Not once a year at a retreat.
Then he sharpens it: what is going on in the part of me they call the ruling part? The Stoics' word was hegemonikon, the steering center of a person, where judgments and choices happen.
He wants to check who's at the wheel. And then the striking part. Whose soul do I have right now?
A child's? A teenager's? A tyrant's?
A farm animal's? A wild beast's? It's almost funny, and it's very honest.
On some days a person might cycle through several: the child who wants it now, the tyrant who wants it done my way, the grazing animal scrolling for the next bite, the wild animal in traffic.
The question isn't a test you pass.

teach.h: A MIRROR TO GLANCE AT OFTEN.
teach.b: It's a mirror you keep glancing at.

teach.h: WHAT AM I USING IT FOR.
teach.b: Each time you ask, you get a little gap: you notice the tyrant, and the noticing can loosen his grip. Asked often enough, it becomes a habit of returning, which was yesterday's whole lesson.
You don't have to fix the answer. Just hear it.

how: Readers of Marcus Aurelius sometimes set reminders to ask the question of Meditations 5.11, 'what am I using my soul for right now?', several times a day.

o: a Greek word for the strongest ruler in a city
the ruling part: the mind's steering center
the gut feeling that acts before you think

games.q: you notice you've spent an hour arguing with strangers online. what does 5.11 ask?
o: what am I using my soul for right now?
how can I make my point sharper?
games.why: Marcus asks on every occasion what his soul is being used for, and whose soul it is at that moment.

practice: Ask it now: what am I using my soul for, right now? Listen for the honest answer, resting, or half here and half in an email.
Then ask lightly whose soul this is at the moment, a child's, a tyrant's, something calmer, and simply name it without judging.

wordCard.voice: Hegemonikon. Marcus's word for the ruling part, the steering center where judgments and choices happen. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek, 'the ruling part': the Stoic name for the mind's steering center, from hegemon, 'leader'.

carryVoice: Your line: what am I using it for. A mirror to glance at, not a test to pass. See you soon.
